quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you traffic only moves in one direction. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow when entering a one-way street.

questions.question: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you can drive in an area.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are bad, such as wet roads or poor visibility.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter noise from larger trucks.
The faster speed of larger trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely. Let pedestrians and other vehicles pass first. Then go when it is safe to continue.

questions.question: If traffic lights are out due to a power outage, you should:

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed when it is your turn. Drive slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Your blind spot is an area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
Can see in your rearview mirror.
Can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas beside and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without moving your head. Always check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn the cyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to get around them.
Slow down and give them plenty of space.
Speed up and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a bicyclist and give them as much space as possible. Bicyclists are not protected like car drivers. Passing too quickly can make them lose control.

questions.question: If your vehicle skids on water, you should quickly apply the brakes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not slam on the brakes. Instead, release the gas pedal and try to regain control. Let the skid stop on its own.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, which must yield?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Normally, vehicles go in the order they arrive at a four-way stop. If two arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Areas around a truck or bus where drivers cannot see other vehicles.
A roadway where stereo volume is restricted.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around a truck or bus where drivers cannot see other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars in these areas cannot be seen. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Which one must you obey over the other three?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over traffic signs, signals, and road markings. Other authorized traffic directors include fire police, highway work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass first.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane to make the turn. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for traffic crossing from other directions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Flaggers control traffic in construction areas.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians that they may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Driving faster is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, water can push your tires up on the surface, causing you to lose control. This is called hydroplaning. To avoid it, slow down when driving in wet conditions.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving disrupts the flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving disrupts the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can disrupt the normal flow of traffic and is illegal. You can be cited for driving too slowly.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, visibility is reduced. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches, you must drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead pass through. There is no cross traffic. What must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
You can roll slowly past the stop sign.
You can follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic. Do not skip your stop just because other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: All motor vehicles in Minnesota must have liability insurance.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. If you cannot show proof to a police officer, your driver license and vehicle registration can be taken away.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. These vehicles travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Can you park in a handicap access aisle next to a handicap parking space?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but you must first check the intersection. Let any pedestrians or traffic still in the intersection pass before you move.

questions.question: Where are solid white stop lines painted across traffic lanes?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right side?

options.text: When the vehicle is turning left and there is an open passing lane.
If it means driving off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is turning left and there is an open passing lane.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right when there is an open passing lane and the vehicle ahead is turning left. You can also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same as driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as alcohol.
questions.explanation: Fatigue affects driving the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs you as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What driving technique helps you avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve grip.
Leave the highways as quickly as possible.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your distance from other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let pedestrians and other traffic pass, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and wait before getting back on.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Take your foot off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and turning slightly. Check for other traffic before steering back on.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. As a driver, you must watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: When a car behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give them space in front to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them space in front to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a car behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass more easily and quickly.

questions.question: When should you drive in a lane with a red X light?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Lane control lights show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means that lane is closed. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

questions.question: Yellow-green signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Yellow-green signs warn about pedestrians, bicycles, and school zones. Drive carefully around these signs.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, always check behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. While backing, turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: You do not need to stay as far behind a motorcycle as you do behind a car.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. Stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to avoid danger.
